recipeIngredient: 3 large carrots, peeled and cut into large chunks
2 stalks of celery, cut into large chunks
half of 1 yellow onion, peeled and cut into large chunks
10 cups chicken or vegetable broth (I use 10 cups water plus 2 tablespoons Better Than Bouillon chicken base)
1 1/2 cups pastina (I use Stelline from the Good and Gather brand at Target)
freshly grated Parmesan cheese for topping

recipeInstructions.text: Heat oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the chunky carrots, celery, onion, and garlic to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes.
recipeInstructions.name: Sauté Veggies

recipeInstructions.text: Add broth and salt. Simmer for 30 minutes, until the vegetables are very tender.
recipeInstructions.name: Simmer

recipeInstructions.text: Use a slotted spoon to transfer the vegetable chunks to a bowl. Set aside to cool for a few minutes (you don’t want to add scorching hot veggies to your plastic blender).
recipeInstructions.name: Remove Veggies

recipeInstructions.text: When the veggies have cooled a bit, blend them with 1-2 cups of broth until very smooth. Add the blended mixture back to the pot; stir to incorporate.
recipeInstructions.name: Blend

recipeInstructions.text: Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain and toss with olive oil and a pinch of salt.
recipeInstructions.name: Pastina

recipeInstructions.text: Put a scoop of pastina in a shallow bowl. Ladle the steaming-hot broth over the top, then top each bowl with freshly grated Parmesan.
recipeInstructions.name: Serve

review.reviewBody:
My son and husband woke up not feeling great this morning and I was running to Walmart anyway, so I decided to pick up the few things I needed to make a batch of this soup today! 

Sadly, they didn't have the pastina pasta, so I used bowtie pasta. I also used chicken bone broth instead of the Bouillon. And I also cooked boneless skinless chicken thighs in with the broth and veggies for some extra protein. 

This was so simple and so delicious. I have a ton to freeze and a ton in the fridge for my boys to eat throughout the week as they work on feeling better. 

Thank you for another winning recipe!

Simply amazing! So much flavor from such simple ingredients. I'm sensitive to garlic and onions so I kept them whole to add flavor to the broth and then discarded them before blending the veggies and the soup still had so much flavor!

I’ve been rocking a cold for the last 1 to 2 weeks but with pregnancy, you don’t get to take anything helpful; finally got a chance to try this, and this hot silky broth is so so good. I gave it a verrrry generous amount of fresh cracked pepper along with the grated Parmesan.
Very good! I had to saute longer.  The only thing is when I blended, I still got a crunch from the celery.

Recently I've been making a version of this on repeat because I love the Progresso Chickarina soup and obsessed with the tiny star pasta but wanted a homemade version without 1000 ingredients lol!  

Of course I should have checked here first! DUH!  I am 100% going to blend the veggies in next time - what a great idea!
What an awesome soup recipe! The family loved it! It will be on repeat in our home especially with the kids asking for more!!! Thank you.

I couldn’t wait to try this soup.  It truly did not disappoint.  I used orzo because that was the smallest pasta that I had in the pantry.  Will be keeping a container in my fridge for quick & healthy lunches.  Thank you for the recipe.
I have made pastina before with broth bu I sure do love the extra step of blended veggies! Brillant. I will make this recipie from now on.

I'm not sick, but I couldn't wait to make this. I had everything except celery, so I substituted a bunch of parsley (which I removed before blending) and half of a green pepper. It's easy and so delicious and comforting, and I usually have these ingredients at home, so it will be in the regular rotation.
Made exactly as written (except used an immersion blender since it's all I have ) and was absolutely delicious! Love how simple it is.

OMG, this reminds me of something my mom would make for me as a child when I was sick. Except hers used condensed cream of celery soup lol. Thanks for bringing the spirit of that dish into the 21st century so that I can share it with my son. :)
